messages:
alex: Quick sync — we wrapped the DB connection storm postmortem. I sketched action items but want to lock owners/timelines and fold the triage commands into the playbook. Can folks ack and take ownership?

maria: Ack. I can own the runbook edits for triage steps. Will add a short checklist and the exact psql commands we used. Target: EOD Tue.

sam: @maria ok with me pairing on the commands. I ran a quick sim of the connection spike yesterday; we should include the `pg_stat_activity` check and the safe terminate pattern.

jenna: I can own escalation path updates (who to page at 20% CPU on primary vs replica). Will draft the on-call decision tree and pager thresholds. ETA Thu COB.

alex: Thanks. Two asks: 1) add the quick mitigation command we ran to free connections, and 2) add a clear fallback policy (switch read traffic to replicas). Maria/sam can you propose concrete commands for the playbook? Jenna, add the PD schedule snippet so SREs know who to call.

maria: Draft commands I'll add to the runbook (will include notes):
```
-- check blockers
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';
-- list long running queries
SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;
-- terminate a blocking backend (use with caution)
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(12345);
```
I'll also include the KB link to the safer termination wrapper script.

sam: Suggest adding the connection-pooler restart command and a small sanity test:
```bash
sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer
curl -sS http://localhost:8000/health || echo 'health failed'
```
I'll open a PR with those snippets and a short caution block about race conditions.

jenna: For escalation: if primary CPU > 20% for 5m, page SRE-Primary; if >40% or replication lag > 5s, page eng-oncall + db-team. I'll add a small flow diagram and the PD escalation snippet.

alex: Great. Two meta items — recurring pattern: similar connection storms popped 3x in last quarter. We should add a recurring incident tracker in the playbook and a telemetry query to detect early. Maria can you add the telemetry SQL to the runbook?

maria: Yep — adding a scheduled query and a Grafana alert sample. Example:
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, max(total_connections) FROM db_connection_metrics GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 30;
```
I'll include threshold guidance.

devops-bot: New PR created by sam: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pull/432 — contains command snippets and tests.

sam: PR linked. @alex @maria tagging for review. I added a small integration test that runs the health checks after pgbouncer restart.

alex: Assigning final reviewers: @maria (runbook content), @jenna (escalation wording). Please merge once CI passes. Also setting an action item tracker row: {owner:maria, item:runbook triage steps + telemetry, due:2026-03-17}, {owner:sam, item:playbook commands + tests, due:2026-03-15}, {owner:jenna, item:escalation flow + PD snippet, due:2026-03-19}.

jenna: I'll also schedule a 30m walkthrough next Fri to orient on-call and CS about the new steps.

maria: Merged a minor doc commit, will finish telemetry + thresholds tomorrow.

incident-bot: Action items updated in incident tracker: https://tracker.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-013/actions

alex: Closing loop — once merged, add a one-paragraph summary to the postmortem and mark remediation status as "in verification". Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: Done — tests passed, PR merged (ran the pgbouncer restart in staging). Noted the race condition caveat in the playbook.

alex: Perfect. Will check back in 2 weeks for verification and recurring alert noise review.
